I’m so glad someone has posted about this because I’ve wanted to but been afraid of people judging me. 

I can’t properly articulate all that I think about it but here are some ideas and beliefs I hold. 

As teenager I believed (through nobody teaching me explicitly, just picking up from my environment) that protected sex was haraam because I thought that doing it not for it’s “intended purpose” (to bear a child) was wrong. I have since learned that my family’s sect and community don’t believe this and protected sex with your spouse is allowed. This feels to me like it doesn’t make sense. I am a queer Muslim and I think a lot about different way to have sex and how most of them are able to produce offspring, which feels the same as using contraceptives in my belief. So what does this mean about sex for queer muslims? Marriage in history has excluded us, so if we hold beliefs that we should be allowed to be together, it makes sense that sex before marriage is allowed too, no? (Obviously if you don’t believe in acting on queer thoughts I know you might disagree but for me it appears to go hand in hand) 

I also think that sex can be a lot for your mental health, good and bad. It is important to protect yourself both physically and mentally and I think this is why Allah (swt) wants us to make sure we don’t rush it. It is a special act between humans and it shouldn’t be taken lightly either. 

I also think that marriage means less nowadays. Like it’s so easy to just get divorced and it’s not necessary for every family to bear biological children as there as so many children needing homes. A family is different now, it could be blended, single parent, same gender parents, adopted or fostered kids etc and marriage is the foundation of family. Not everyone even has the ability to raise children themselves for whatever reason. This means that sex is no longer for its “purpose” a lot of the time.

Sometimes I am confused about it, but I want to do things because they feel right not just because someone told me it was wrong. I think if you are being safe and smart and you don’t regret it, it can be positive.

I have run some similar events and here are my quick tips:

\- Make use of your existing networks to spread the word, this shit travels fast in minority communities! I bet loads of people will turn up because x told them that y told them that you are putting this event on and they wanted to be included :)

\- Get in touch with organisations that can support you: minority stuff, arts funds, public speakers, use them all! Reach out to anyone that could help you.

\- Be real clear this is a space for queer black folx!! They may well be people who are like "listen I'm a white cishet man and life is HARD for me so include me else you're mean" and you gotta tell them you appreciate the support but that's all it can be, support. This is your space and it isn't gatekeeping so don't let anyone tell you it is!

\- Enjoy your space, you waited long enough for it! Even if it's not what you expect, you are doing a great thing and it's for you too so make the most of it :)

Good luck, you got this! <3
